# Introduction

Particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometres (PM2.5) is one of the most
harmful air pollutants — small enough to enter the bloodstream and cause
cardiovascular and respiratory disease. Delhi consistently ranks among the most
polluted cities in the world, with winter months (October–January) seeing
PM2.5 concentrations far exceeding WHO safe limits.

This vignette demonstrates how the `vayuayan` package can be used to combine
two independent data sources — satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates from
Washington University (WUSTL ACAG) and ground-level CPCB monitoring station
readings — to analyse Delhi's air quality in 2023. We also investigate a
critical policy question: are the existing 40 CPCB monitoring stations
distributed well enough to capture the full spatial extent of pollution, or
are there under-monitored regions where PM2.5 is being systematically missed?

---

# Data & methods

## Satellite data

Monthly PM2.5 estimates are sourced from the Washington University in St. Louis
Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group (WUSTL ACAG) V6.GL.02.04 product. This
dataset provides gridded PM2.5 concentrations at approximately 0.01° resolution
(~1km), derived from a combination of satellite aerosol optical depth retrievals,
chemical transport modelling, and ground-based calibration.

Files are downloaded as NetCDF (`.nc`) format using the `pm25_download_netcdf()`
function in `vayuayan`.

## Ground data (CPCB)

Daily PM2.5 readings from the Central Pollution Control Board's Continuous
Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) are fetched using the
`cpcb_download_city_data()` function. Delhi has 40 operational monitoring
stations managed by DPCC, CPCB, IMD, and IITM.

## Comparison caveat

The satellite data represents a **spatial mean over an area** (the Delhi
GeoJSON boundary), whereas CPCB data is a **point-source average** across
monitoring stations. Some divergence is expected due to this point-to-area
difference. Additionally, CPCB data is real-time/daily while satellite data
is a monthly mean — ground data is aggregated to monthly means for fair
comparison.

# Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
  vayuayan,
  tidyverse,
  tidylog,
  terra,
  sf,
  tidyterra,
  exactextractr,
  gstat,
  sp,
  ggview
)
```

# Results

## 1. Seasonal trend: ground vs satellite PM2.5

```{r ground-data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Get Delhi city-level ground data
delhi_ground <- cpcb_download_city_data(
  city          = "Delhi",
  year          = 2023,
  save_location = "delhi_aqi_2023.csv"
)

# Load and reshape wide → long
delhi_wide <- read.csv("delhi_aqi_2023.csv")

delhi_ground <- delhi_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Day,
    names_to  = "Month_Name",
    values_to = "ground_pm25"
  ) %>%
  mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(ground_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

print(delhi_ground)
```

```{r satellite-data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")

delhi_sat_results <- lapply(1:12, function(m) {
  stats <- pm25_get_stats(
    geojson_file = delhi_geojson,
    year         = 2023,
    month        = m
  )
  data.frame(month = m, sat_pm25 = stats$mean)
})

delhi_sat_df <- do.call(rbind, delhi_sat_results)
delhi_final <- inner_join(delhi_ground, delhi_sat_df, by = "month")

print(delhi_final)
```

```{r line-chart, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
ggplot(delhi_final, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)"),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)"), size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "CPCB Ground"               = "#d77027ff",
    "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)" = "#4575b4"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Delhi 2023: PM2.5 Satellite vs CPCB Ground Estimates",
    y     = expression(paste("PM2.5 Concentration (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),
    x     = NULL,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

> **Note:** For 2024 and 2025, ground data is available but the satellite
> component is pending the official NetCDF release from Washington University.

---

## 2. Spatial distribution: PM2.5 heatmap (November 2023)

November represents peak pollution season in Delhi due to crop burning,
Diwali firecrackers, and temperature inversion trapping pollutants near the surface.

```{r heatmap, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")
delhi_shape <- st_read(delhi_geojson, quiet = TRUE)
nov_raster <- rast("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.202311-202311.nc")
delhi_raster <- crop(nov_raster, vect(delhi_shape))
delhi_raster_mask <- mask(delhi_raster, vect(delhi_shape))

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = delhi_raster_mask) +
  geom_sf(
    data      = delhi_shape,
    fill      = NA,
    color     = "royalblue4",
    linewidth = 0.65
  ) +
  scale_fill_whitebox_c(
    palette = "muted",
    name    = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")"))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Spatial Distribution of PM2.5 in Delhi",
    subtitle = "Satellite Estimate: November 2023",
    caption  = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V6.GL.02.04"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

---

## 3. Station network: choropleth + CPCB locations

```{r station-list, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Get station list
delhi_station_list <- cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi")

# Add coordinates via OpenStreetMap geocoding
# Cached to CSV to avoid re-geocoding on every render (~40 seconds)
if (file.exists("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv")) {
  delhi_station_list <- read.csv("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv")
} else {
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(delhi_station_list)
  write.csv(delhi_station_list, "delhi_stations_with_coords.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}

delhi_full_sf <- st_as_sf(
  delhi_station_list,
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs    = 4326
)

print(delhi_station_list[, c("value", "label", "lat", "lon")])
```

```{r choropleth, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")
delhi_districts <- st_read(delhi_geojson, quiet = TRUE)
nov_raster <- rast("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.202311-202311.nc")

district_means <- terra::extract(nov_raster, vect(delhi_districts),
  fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE
)
delhi_districts$sat_pm25 <- district_means[, 2]

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data      = delhi_districts,
    aes(fill = sat_pm25),
    color     = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = delhi_full_sf,
    color = "royalblue4",
    size  = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", direction = -1) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi District-Wise PM2.5 Choropleth",
    subtitle = "District colors = Satellite Average | Blue dots = CPCB Station Locations",
    caption  = "Do districts with more dots show better ground-satellite alignment?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

---

## 4. Monitoring gap analysis: where are sensors missing pollution?

A key limitation of ground-based monitoring is spatial coverage. The 40 CPCB
stations are not uniformly distributed across Delhi — some districts have
multiple stations while others have none. This raises an important policy
question: **in districts with no sensors, does satellite data suggest pollution
levels are being underestimated?**

To answer this, we interpolate ground PM2.5 readings across Delhi using
Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) — a fast spatial interpolation method that
estimates values at unsampled locations based on nearby station readings.
The delta (satellite − IDW ground) reveals where the sensor network may be
missing pollution.

```{r winter-ground, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Download winter (Oct-Jan) per-station PM2.5
if (!dir.exists("station_data")) dir.create("station_data")

station_raw <- lapply(seq_along(delhi_station_list$value), function(i) {
  id <- delhi_station_list$value[i]
  file <- paste0("station_data/", id, ".csv")

  tryCatch(
    {
      if (!file.exists(file)) {
        cpcb_download_station_data(
          station_id    = id,
          year          = 2023,
          save_location = file
        )
      }
      df <- read.csv(file)

      df %>%
        pivot_longer(cols = -Day, names_to = "Month_Name", values_to = "pm25") %>%
        mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%
        filter(month %in% c(1, 10, 11, 12), !is.na(pm25)) %>%
        summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
        mutate(value = id)
    },
    error = function(e) {
      data.frame(value = id, ground_pm25 = NA)
    }
  )
})

station_ground <- do.call(rbind, station_raw)

# Join with coords
station_ground_sf <- station_ground %>%
  filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%
  left_join(
    delhi_station_list %>% select(value, lat, lon),
    by = "value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cat(nrow(station_ground_sf), "stations with valid winter PM2.5\n")
```

```{r winter-raster, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Build winter average satellite raster (Oct-Jan)
winter_rasters <- rast(lapply(c(1, 10, 11, 12), function(m) {
  rast(sprintf("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.2023%02d-2023%02d.nc", m, m))
}))
winter_raster <- mean(winter_rasters)

delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")
delhi_shape_union <- st_read(delhi_geojson, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_union()
winter_delhi <- crop(winter_raster, vect(delhi_shape_union))
winter_delhi <- mask(winter_delhi, vect(delhi_shape_union))

# District winter means for choropleth base
delhi_districts$winter_sat_pm25 <- exact_extract(
  winter_delhi, delhi_districts, "mean"
)
```

```{r idw, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Project to UTM zone 43N for distance-based interpolation
station_utm <- st_transform(station_ground_sf, crs = 32643)
delhi_utm <- st_transform(st_as_sf(delhi_shape_union), crs = 32643)

# 1km prediction grid over Delhi
bbox <- st_bbox(delhi_utm)
grid_sf <- expand.grid(
  x = seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], by = 1000),
  y = seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], by = 1000)
) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32643) %>%
  st_filter(delhi_utm)

# IDW interpolation (idp=2: inverse square distance weighting)
station_sp <- as(station_utm, "Spatial")
grid_sp <- as(grid_sf, "Spatial")
idw_out <- idw(ground_pm25 ~ 1, station_sp, grid_sp, idp = 2)

# Convert to raster
idw_sf <- st_as_sf(idw_out) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326)
idw_rast <- rasterize(vect(idw_sf), winter_delhi, field = "var1.pred")
```

```{r delta-map, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Delta = satellite - IDW interpolated ground
delta_rast <- winter_delhi - idw_rast
delta_rast <- mask(delta_rast, vect(delhi_shape_union))

delta_df <- as.data.frame(delta_rast, xy = TRUE) %>%
  rename(delta = 3) %>%
  filter(!is.na(delta))

ggplot() +
  # Base: district satellite PM2.5
  geom_sf(
    data      = delhi_districts,
    aes(fill = winter_sat_pm25),
    color     = "white",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  # Delta overlay
  geom_raster(
    data  = delta_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = delta),
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # CPCB station locations
  geom_sf(
    data  = station_ground_sf,
    color = "black",
    fill  = "yellow",
    size  = 3,
    shape = 21,
    alpha = 0.95
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = "#2166ac",
    mid      = "#f7f7f7",
    high     = "#d6604d",
    midpoint = 0,
    name     = expression(paste(Delta ~ PM[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi Winter 2023: Where Are Sensors Missing Pollution?",
    subtitle = "Red = satellite sees more pollution than ground sensors capture\nBlue = sensors overestimate | Yellow = CPCB station locations",
    caption  = "Delta = satellite − IDW interpolated ground | Winter avg Oct–Jan 2023\nSource: WUSTL ACAG V6.GL.02.04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

---

# Discussion

The seasonal trend analysis confirms Delhi's well-documented pollution pattern —
PM2.5 peaks sharply in November–January driven by crop residue burning in
neighbouring states, temperature inversions, and reduced wind speeds. Satellite
and ground estimates broadly agree on this seasonality, though ground readings
are consistently higher than satellite estimates, likely due to the point-to-area
comparison caveat noted in the Methods section.

The spatial heatmap (November 2023) reveals that pollution is not uniform across
Delhi — northwestern and outer districts tend to show elevated PM2.5 relative to
the central areas, though variation exists at fine spatial scales that the 40-station
network may not fully capture.

The monitoring gap analysis (delta map) provides the most policy-relevant finding:
districts shown in red have satellite-estimated PM2.5 significantly higher than
what the nearest ground station records. These are regions where the existing
monitoring network may be providing an incomplete picture of actual population
exposure — not necessarily because air is cleaner there, but because sensors
are sparse. This finding can inform decisions about where new CAAQMS stations
should be prioritised.
